{"confidence":"medium","events":[{"actor_id":"EO:14117","char_end":10384,"char_start":3253,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"parent_as_amended","id":"CHAIN:EO:14110#1","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Section 1. Policy. It is the policy of the United States to restrict access \nby countries of concern to Americans’ bulk sensitive personal data and \nUnited States Government-related data when such access would pose an \nunacceptable risk to the national security of the United States. At the same \ntime, the United States continues to support open, global, interoperable, \nreliable, and secure flows of data across borders, as well as maintaining \nvital consumer, economic, scientific, and trade relationships that the United \nStates has with other countries. \nThe continuing effort by countries of concern to access Americans’ bulk \nsensitive personal data and United States Government-related data threatens \nthe national security and foreign policy of the United States. Such countries’ \ngovernments may seek to access and use sensitive personal data in a manner \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 22:57 Feb 29, 2024 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01MRE0.SGM 01MRE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 2 of 10 ===\n15422 Federal Register / Vol. 89, No. 42 / Friday, March 1, 2024 / Presidential Documents \nthat is not in accordance with democratic values, safeguards for privacy, \nand other human rights and freedoms. Such countries’ approach stands \nin sharp contrast to the practices of democracies with respect to sensitive \npersonal data and principles reflected in the Organisation for Economic \nCo-operation and Development Declaration on Government Access to Per-\nsonal Data Held by Private Sector Entities. Unrestricted transfers of Ameri-\ncans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government-related \ndata to such countries of concern may therefore enable them to exploit \nsuch data for a variety of nefarious purposes, including to engage in malicious \ncyber-enabled activities. Countries of concern can use their access to Ameri-\ncans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government-related \ndata to track and build profiles on United States individuals, including \nFederal employees and contractors, for illicit purposes, including blackmail \nand espionage. Access to Americans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United \nStates Government-related data by countries of concern through data \nbrokerages, third-party vendor agreements, employment agreements, invest-\nment agreements, or other such arrangements poses particular and unaccept-\nable risks to our national security given that these arrangements often can \nprovide countries of concern with direct and unfettered access to Americans’ \nbulk sensitive personal data. Countries of concern can use access to United \nStates persons’ bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government- \nrelated data to collect information on activists, academics, journalists, dis-\nsidents, political figures, or members of non-governmental organizations or \nmarginalized communities in order to intimidate such persons; curb dissent \nor political opposition; otherwise limit freedoms of expression, peaceful \nassembly, or association; or enable other forms of suppression of civil lib-\nerties. \nThis risk of access to Americans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United \nStates Government-related data is not limited to direct access by countries \nof concern. Entities owned by, and entities or individuals controlled by \nor subject to the jurisdiction or direction of, a country of concern may \nenable the government of a country of concern to indirectly access such \ndata. For example, a country of concern may have cyber, national security, \nor intelligence laws that, without sufficient legal safeguards, obligate such \nentities and individuals to provide that country’s intelligence services access \nto Americans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government- \nrelated data. \nThese risks may be exacerbated when countries of concern use bulk sensitive \npersonal data to develop AI capabilities and algorithms that, in turn, enable \nthe use of large datasets in increasingly sophisticated and effective ways \nto the detriment of United States national security. Countries of concern \ncan use AI to target United States persons for espionage or blackmail by, \nfor example, recognizing patterns across multiple unrelated datasets to iden-\ntify potential individuals whose links to the Federal Government would \nbe otherwise obscured in a single dataset. \nWhile aspects of this threat have been addressed in previous executive \nactions, such as Executive Order 13694 of April 1, 2015 (Blocking the \nProperty of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled \nActivities), as amended, additional steps need to be taken to address this \nthreat. \nAt the same time, the United States is committed to promoting an open, \nglobal, interoperable, reliable, and secure Internet; protecting human rights \nonline and offline; supporting a vibrant, global economy by promoting cross- \nborder data flows required to enable international commerce and trade; \nand facilitating open investment. To ensure that the United States continues \nto meet these important policy objectives, this order does not authorize \nthe imposition of generalized data localization requirements to store Ameri-\ncans’ bulk sensitive personal data or United States Government-related data \nwithin the United States or to locate computing facilities used to process \nAmericans’ bulk sensitive personal data or United States Government-related \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 22:57 Feb 29, 2024 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01MRE0.SGM 01MRE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 3 of 10 ===\n15423 Federal Register / Vol. 89, No. 42 / Friday, March 1, 2024 / Presidential Documents \ndata within the United States. This order also does not broadly prohibit \nUnited States persons from conducting commercial transactions, including \nexchanging financial and other data as part of the sale of commercial goods \nand services, with entities and individuals located in or subject to the \ncontrol, direction, or jurisdiction of countries of concern, or impose measures \naimed at a broader decoupling of the substantial consumer, economic, sci-\nentific, and trade relationships that the United States has with other countries. \nIn addition, my Administration has made commitments to increase public \naccess to the results of taxpayer-funded scientific research, the sharing and \ninteroperability of electronic health information, and patient access to their \ndata. The national security restrictions established in this order are specific, \ncarefully calibrated actions to minimize the risks associated with access \nto bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government-related data \nby countries of concern while minimizing disruption to commercial activity. \nThis order shall be implemented consistent with these policy objectives, \nincluding by tailoring any regulations issued and actions taken pursuant \nto this order to address the national security threat posed by access to \nAmericans’ bulk sensitive personal data and United States Government- \nrelated data by countries of concern.","sections_touched":["Section 1"],"signing_date":"2024-02-28","source":{"filing_date":null,"location_confidence":"high","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"89 FR 15421, PDF pages 1-10","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"ba21fdd74728be89271083248554b507b06e314bfcffba02554b1f08f3dadb9c","signing_date":"2024-02-28","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14117.txt","text_sha256":"356519c03acd1192515d84aeeca3ecd6f4861b40b160c2ad37d51718cfe9ed38","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-03-01/pdf/2024-04573.pdf"},"verb":"transfer"},{"actor_id":"EO:14144","char_end":54345,"char_start":53225,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"parent_as_amended","id":"CHAIN:EO:14110#2","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Because I find that additional steps must be taken to deal with \nthe national emergency with respect to significant malicious cyber-enabled \nactivities declared in Executive Order 13694 of April 1, 2015 (Blocking \nthe Property of Certain Persons Engaging in Significant Malicious Cyber- \nEnabled Activities), as amended by Executive Order 13757 of December \n28, 2016 (Taking Additional Steps to Address the National Emergency With \nRespect to Significant Malicious Cyber-Enabled Activities), and further \namended by Executive Order 13984 of January 19, 2021 (Taking Additional \nSteps to Address the National Emergency With Respect to Significant Mali-\ncious Cyber-Enabled Activities), to protect against the growing and evolving \nthreat of malicious cyber-enabled activities against the United States and \nUnited States allies and partners, including the increasing threats by foreign \nactors of unauthorized access to critical infrastructure, ransomware, and \ncyber-enabled intrusions and sanctions evasion, I hereby order that section \n1(a) of Executive Order 13694 is further amended to read as follows: \n‘‘Section 1.","sections_touched":["section \n1(a)","Section 1"],"signing_date":"2025-01-16","source":{"filing_date":null,"location_confidence":"high","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"90 FR 6755, PDF pages 1-17","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"006cddd54c6f3aeb42eb0ca48b36a692c13ad47d01c91ad47e7e07a99c82691d","signing_date":"2025-01-16","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14144.txt","text_sha256":"7aca76eea4b17e70b4cfa07706df3f6c544da4fc1f58c5cbee8917441f3bcd8b","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-17/pdf/2025-01470.pdf"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:14148","char_end":10886,"char_start":1905,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:14110#3","notes":"Change wording lead; (a) The APST, the Special \nAdvisor for AI and Crypto, and the APNSA shall immediately review, in \ncoordination with the heads of all agencies as they deem relevant, all policies, \ndirectives, regulations, orders, and other actions taken pursuant to the re-\nvoked Executive Order 14110 of October 30, 2023 (Safe, Secure, and Trust-\nworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence). The APST, the Spe-\ncial Advisor for AI and Crypto, and the APNSA shall, in coordination \nwith the heads of relevant agencies, identify any actions taken pursuant \nto Executive Order 14110 that are or may be inconsistent with, or present \nobstacles to, the policy set forth in section 2 of this order. For any such \nagency actions identified, the heads of agencies shall, as appropriate and \nconsistent with applicable law, suspend, revise, or rescind such actions, \nor propose suspending, revising, or rescinding such actions. If in any case \nsuch suspension, revision, or rescission cannot be finalized immediately, \nthe APST and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to provide \nall available exemptions authorized by any such orders, rules, regulations, \nguidelines, or policies, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, \nuntil such action can be finalized.","sections_touched":["section 2"],"signing_date":"2025-01-23","source":{"filing_date":null,"location_confidence":"high","location_verified":false,"page_or_item":"90 FR 8741, PDF pages 1-2","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"332b46f8cf4f4e7ed120a8092f14389640ada7538c65debc6fb3733298a5959e","signing_date":"2025-01-23","text_path":"jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14179.txt","text_sha256":"2b16b065cdadba70b8ff841a3d49e5305150fb91741a6b8098811cbb25bc56a7","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-01-31/pdf/2025-02172.pdf"},"verb":"revoke"},{"actor_id":"EO:14306","char_end":10054,"char_start":9509,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"parent_as_amended","id":"CHAIN:EO:14110#5","notes":"Change wording lead; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"Executive Order 13960 of December 3, 2020 (Promoting the Use of Trust-\nworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Government), and section \n4(b) of Executive Order 14091; \n(ii) the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers’ roles, responsibilities, senior-\nity, position, and reporting structures; \n(iii) for the agencies identified in 31 U.S.C. 901(b), the creation of internal \nArtificial Intelligence Governance Boards, or other appropriate mecha-\nnisms, at each agency within 60 days of the issuance of the guidance \nto coordinate and govern AI issues through relevant senior leaders from \nacross the agency; \n(iv) required minimum risk-management practices for Government uses \nof AI that impact people’s rights or safety, including, where appropriate, \nthe following practices derived from OSTP’s Blueprint for an AI Bill \nof Rights and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework: conducting public \nconsultation; assessing data quality; assessing and mitigating disparate \nimpacts and algorithmic discrimination; providing notice of the use of \nAI; continuously monitoring and evaluating deployed AI; and granting \nhuman consideration and remedies for adverse decisions made using AI; \n(v) specific Federal Government uses of AI that are presumed by default \nto impact rights or safety; \n(vi) recommendations to agencies to reduce barriers to the responsible \nuse of AI, including barriers related to information technology infrastruc-\nture, data, workforce, budgetary restrictions, and cybersecurity processes; \n(vii) requirements that agencies identified in 31 U.S.C. 901(b) develop \nAI strategies and pursue high-impact AI use cases; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 23:02 Oct 31, 2023 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00030 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01NOE0.SGM 01NOE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 29 of 36 ===\n75219 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 210 / Wednesday, November 1, 2023 / Presidential Documents \n(viii) in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of \nHomeland Security, and the heads of other appropriate agencies as deter-\nmined by the Director of OMB, recommendations to agencies regarding: \n(A) external testing for AI, including AI red-teaming for generative AI, \nto be developed in coordination with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure \nSecurity Agency; \n(B) testing and safeguards against discriminatory, misleading, inflam-\nmatory, unsafe, or deceptive outputs, as well as against producing child \nsexual abuse material and against producing non-consensual intimate im-\nagery of real individuals (including intimate digital depictions of the body \nor body parts of an identifiable individual), for generative AI; \n(C) reasonable steps to watermark or otherwise label output from genera-\ntive AI; \n(D) application of the mandatory minimum risk-management practices \ndefined under subsection 10.1(b)(iv) of this section to procured AI; \n(E) independent evaluation of vendors’ claims concerning both the effec-\ntiveness and risk mitigation of their AI offerings; \n(F) documentation and oversight of procured AI; \n(G) maximizing the value to agencies when relying on contractors to \nuse and enrich Federal Government data for the purposes of AI develop-\nment and operation; \n(H) provision of incentives for the continuous improvement of procured \nAI; and \n(I) training on AI in accordance with the principles set out in this \norder and in other references related to AI listed herein; and \n(ix) requirements for public reporting on compliance with this guidance."},{"char_end":120156,"char_start":119789,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":120156,"context_char_start":119789,"line":1739,"pdf_page":29,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(a) Within 45 days of the date \nof this order, to plan a national surge in AI talent in the Federal Government, \nthe Director of OSTP and the Director of OMB, in consultation with the \nAssistant to the President for National Security Affairs, the Assistant to \nthe President for Economic Policy, the Assistant to the President and Domes-\ntic Policy Advisor, and the Assistant to the President and Director of the \nGender Policy Council, shall identify priority mission areas for increased \nFederal Government AI talent, the types of talent that are highest priority \nto recruit and develop to ensure adequate implementation of this order \nand use of relevant enforcement and regulatory authorities to address AI \nrisks, and accelerated hiring pathways."},{"char_end":128531,"char_start":127693,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":128531,"context_char_start":127693,"line":1850,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"(b) Within 45 days of the date of this order, to coordinate rapid advances \nin the capacity of the Federal AI workforce, the Assistant to the President \nand Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy, in coordination with the Director \nof OSTP and the Director of OMB, and in consultation with the National \nCyber Director, shall convene an AI and Technology Talent Task Force, \nwhich shall include the Director of OPM, the Director of the General Services \nAdministration’s Technology Transformation Services, a representative from \nthe Chief Human Capital Officers Council, the Assistant to the President \nfor Presidential Personnel, members of appropriate agency technology talent \nprograms, a representative of the Chief Data Officer Council, and a representa-\ntive of the interagency council convened under subsection 10.1(a) of this \nsection."},{"char_end":129601,"char_start":128532,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":129601,"context_char_start":128532,"line":1861,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Task Force’s purpose shall be to accelerate and track the hiring \nof AI and AI-enabling talent across the Federal Government, including \nthrough the following actions: \n(i) within 180 days of the date of this order, tracking and reporting \nprogress to the President on increasing AI capacity across the Federal \nGovernment, including submitting to the President a report and rec-\nommendations for further increasing capacity; \n(ii) identifying and circulating best practices for agencies to attract, hire, \nretain, train, and empower AI talent, including diversity, inclusion, and \naccessibility best practices, as well as to plan and budget adequately \nfor AI workforce needs; \n(iii) coordinating, in consultation with the Director of OPM, the use of \nfellowship programs and agency technology-talent programs and human- \ncapital teams to build hiring capabilities, execute hires, and place AI \ntalent to fill staffing gaps; and \n(iv) convening a cross-agency forum for ongoing collaboration between \nAI professionals to share best practices and improve retention."},{"char_end":130290,"char_start":129603,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":130290,"context_char_start":129603,"line":1878,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(c) Within 45 days of the date of this order, to advance existing Federal \ntechnology talent programs, the United States Digital Service, Presidential \nInnovation Fellowship, United States Digital Corps, OPM, and technology \ntalent programs at agencies, with support from the AI and Technology Talent \nTask Force described in subsection 10.2(b) of this section, as appropriate \nand permitted by law, shall develop and begin to implement plans to support \nthe rapid recruitment of individuals as part of a Federal Government-wide \nAI talent surge to accelerate the placement of key AI and AI-enabling talent \nin high-priority areas and to advance agencies’ data and technology strategies."},{"char_end":133646,"char_start":130292,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":133646,"context_char_start":130292,"line":1887,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"(d) To meet the critical hiring need for qualified personnel to execute \nthe initiatives in this order, and to improve Federal hiring practices for \nAI talent, the Director of OPM, in consultation with the Director of OMB, \nshall: \n(i) within 60 days of the date of this order, conduct an evidence-based \nreview on the need for hiring and workplace flexibility, including Federal \nGovernment-wide direct-hire authority for AI and related data-science and \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 23:02 Oct 31, 2023 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00033 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01NOE0.SGM 01NOE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 32 of 36 ===\n75222 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 210 / Wednesday, November 1, 2023 / Presidential Documents \ntechnical roles, and, where the Director of OPM finds such authority \nis appropriate, grant it; this review shall include the following job series \nat all General Schedule (GS) levels: IT Specialist (2210), Computer Scientist \n(1550), Computer Engineer (0854), and Program Analyst (0343) focused \non AI, and any subsequently developed job series derived from these \njob series; \n(ii) within 60 days of the date of this order, consider authorizing the \nuse of excepted service appointments under 5 CFR 213.3102(i)(3) to address \nthe need for hiring additional staff to implement directives of this order; \n(iii) within 90 days of the date of this order, coordinate a pooled-hiring \naction informed by subject-matter experts and using skills-based assess-\nments to support the recruitment of AI talent across agencies; \n(iv) within 120 days of the date of this order, as appropriate and permitted \nby law, issue guidance for agency application of existing pay flexibilities \nor incentive pay programs for AI, AI-enabling, and other key technical \npositions to facilitate appropriate use of current pay incentives; \n(v) within 180 days of the date of this order, establish guidance and \npolicy on skills-based, Federal Government-wide hiring of AI, data, and \ntechnology talent in order to increase access to those with nontraditional \nacademic backgrounds to Federal AI, data, and technology roles; \n(vi) within 180 days of the date of this order, establish an interagency \nworking group, staffed with both human-resources professionals and re-\ncruiting technical experts, to facilitate Federal Government-wide hiring \nof people with AI and other technical skills; \n(vii) within 180 days of the date of this order, review existing Executive \nCore Qualifications (ECQs) for Senior Executive Service (SES) positions \ninformed by data and AI literacy competencies and, within 365 days \nof the date of this order, implement new ECQs as appropriate in the \nSES assessment process; \n(viii) within 180 days of the date of this order, complete a review of \ncompetencies for civil engineers (GS–0810 series) and, if applicable, other \nrelated occupations, and make recommendations for ensuring that adequate \nAI expertise and credentials in these occupations in the Federal Govern-\nment reflect the increased use of AI in critical infrastructure; ## Valla review leads and component attestations

Review lead only. Every case needs separate applicability, earlier-ending, scope, independent-command, savings and independent whole-case review.
Preparation attestations never approve legal conclusions or replace whole-case review.

sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"Each agency shall, as appropriate and consistent with applica-\nble law: \n(i) identify, analyze, and address disproportionate and adverse human \nhealth and environmental effects (including risks) and hazards of Federal \nactivities, including those related to climate change and cumulative impacts \nof environmental and other burdens on communities with environmental \njustice concerns; \n(ii) evaluate relevant legal authorities and, as available and appropriate, \ntake steps to address disproportionate and adverse human health and \nenvironmental effects (including risks) and hazards unrelated to Federal \nactivities, including those related to climate change and cumulative impacts \nof environmental and other burdens on communities with environmental \njustice concerns; \n(iii) identify, analyze, and address historical inequities, systemic barriers, \nor actions related to any Federal regulation, policy, or practice that impair \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 15:47 Apr 25, 2023 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\26APE0.SGM 26APE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 4 of 11 ===\n25254 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 80 / Wednesday, April 26, 2023 / Presidential Documents \nthe ability of communities with environmental justice concerns to achieve \nor maintain a healthy and sustainable environment; \n(iv) identify, analyze, and address barriers related to Federal activities \nthat impair the ability of communities with environmental justice concerns \nto receive equitable access to human health or environmental benefits, \nincluding benefits related to natural disaster recovery and climate mitiga-\ntion, adaptation, and resilience; \n(v) evaluate relevant legal authorities and, as available and appropriate, \ntake steps to provide, in consultation with unions and employers, opportu-\nnities for workforce training and to support the creation of high-quality \nand well-paying jobs, including union jobs, for people who are part of \ncommunities with environmental justice concerns; \n(vi) evaluate relevant legal authorities and, where available and appropriate, \nconsider adopting or requiring measures to avoid, minimize, or mitigate \ndisproportionate and adverse human health and environmental effects \n(including risks) and hazards of Federal activities on communities with \nenvironmental justice concerns, to the maximum extent practicable, and \nto address any contribution of such Federal activities to adverse effects— \nincluding cumulative impacts of environmental and other burdens—already \nexperienced by such communities; \n(vii) provide opportunities for the meaningful engagement of persons and \ncommunities with environmental justice concerns who are potentially af-\nfected by Federal activities, including by: \n(A) providing timely opportunities for members of the public to share \ninformation or concerns and participate in decision-making processes; \n(B) fully considering public input provided as part of decision-making \nprocesses; \n(C) seeking out and encouraging the involvement of persons and commu-\nnities potentially affected by Federal activities by: \n(1) ensuring that agencies offer or provide information on a Federal \nactivity in a manner that provides meaningful access to individuals \nwith limited English proficiency and is accessible to individuals with \ndisabilities; \n(2) providing notice of and engaging in outreach to communities or \ngroups of people who are potentially affected and who are not regular \nparticipants in Federal decision-making; and \n(3) addressing, to the extent practicable and appropriate, other barriers \nto participation that individuals may face; and \n(D) providing technical assistance, tools, and resources to assist in facili-\ntating meaningful and informed public participation, whenever practicable \nand appropriate; \n(viii) continue to engage in consultation on Federal activities that have \nTribal implications and potentially affect human health or the environment, \npursuant to Executive Order 13175 of November 6, 2000 (Consultation \nand Coordination With Indian Tribal Governments), the Presidential Memo-\nrandum of January 26, 2021 (Tribal Consultation and Strengthening Nation- \nto-Nation Relationships), and the Presidential Memorandum of November \n30, 2022 (Uniform Standards for Tribal Consultation), and fulfill obligations \nestablished pursuant to Executive Order 13007 of May 24, 1996 (Indian \nSacred Sites); \n(ix) carry out environmental reviews under the National Environmental \nPolicy Act (NEPA), 42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq., consistent with the statute \nand its implementing regulations and through the exercise of the agency’s \nexpertise and technical judgment, in a manner that: \n(A) analyzes direct, indirect, and cumulative effects of Federal actions \non communities with environmental justice concerns; \n(B) considers best available science and information on any disparate \nhealth effects (including risks) arising from exposure to pollution and \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 15:47 Apr 25, 2023 Jkt 259001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\26APE0.SGM 26APE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 5 of 11 ===\n25255 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 80 / Wednesday, April 26, 2023 / Presidential Documents \nother environmental hazards, such as information related to the race, \nnational origin, socioeconomic status, age, disability, and sex of the individ-\nuals exposed; and \n(C) provides opportunities for early and meaningful involvement in \nthe environmental review process by communities with environmental \njustice concerns potentially affected by a proposed action, including when \nestablishing or revising agency procedures under NEPA; \n(x) in accordance with Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, 42 U.S.C. \n2000d, and agency regulations, ensure that all programs or activities receiv-\ning Federal financial assistance that potentially affect human health or \nthe environment do not directly, or through contractual or other arrange-\nments, use criteria, policies, practices, or methods of administration that \ndiscriminate on the basis of race, color, or national origin; \n(xi) ensure that the public, including members of communities with envi-\nronmental justice concerns, has adequate access to information on Federal \nactivities, including planning, regulatory actions, implementation, permit-\nting, compliance, and enforcement related to human health or the environ-\nment, when required under the Freedom of Information Act, 5 U.S.C. \n552; the Government in the Sunshine Act, 5 U.S.C. 552b; the Clean Air \nAct, 42 U.S.C. 7401 et seq.; the Clean Water Act, 33 U.S.C. 1251 et \nseq.; the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act of 1986 \n(EPCRA), 42 U.S.C. 11001 et seq.; or other environmental statutes with \npublic information provisions; \n(xii) improve collaboration and communication with State, Tribal, terri-\ntorial, and local governments on programs and activities to advance envi-\nronmental justice; \n(xiii) encourage and, to the extent permitted by law, ensure that Govern-\nment-owned, contractor-operated facilities take appropriate steps to imple-\nment the directives of this order; \n(xiv) consider ways to encourage and, as appropriate, ensure that recipients \nof Federal funds—including recipients of block grant funding—and entities \nsubject to contractual, licensing, or other arrangements with Federal agen-\ncies advance environmental justice; \n(xv) develop internal mechanisms to achieve the goals of this order, includ-\ning by: \n(A) creating performance metrics and other means of accountability; \n(B) identifying and dedicating staff, funding, and other resources; and \n(C) providing appropriate professional development and training of agen-\ncy staff; and \n(xvi) consistent with section 2–2 of Executive Order 12898, ensure that \nFederal activities do not have the effect of: \n(A) excluding persons, including populations, from participation in Fed-\neral activities on the basis of their race, color, or national origin; \n(B) denying persons, including populations, the benefits of Federal activi-\nties on the basis of their race, color, or national origin; or \n(C) subjecting persons, including populations, to discrimination on the \nbasis of their race, color, or national verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"Executive Order 13960 of December 3, 2020 (Promoting the Use of Trust-\nworthy Artificial Intelligence in the Federal Government), and section \n4(b) of Executive Order 14091; \n(ii) the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officers’ roles, responsibilities, senior-\nity, position, and reporting structures; \n(iii) for the agencies identified in 31 U.S.C. 901(b), the creation of internal \nArtificial Intelligence Governance Boards, or other appropriate mecha-\nnisms, at each agency within 60 days of the issuance of the guidance \nto coordinate and govern AI issues through relevant senior leaders from \nacross the agency; \n(iv) required minimum risk-management practices for Government uses \nof AI that impact people’s rights or safety, including, where appropriate, \nthe following practices derived from OSTP’s Blueprint for an AI Bill \nof Rights and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework: conducting public \nconsultation; assessing data quality; assessing and mitigating disparate \nimpacts and algorithmic discrimination; providing notice of the use of \nAI; continuously monitoring and evaluating deployed AI; and granting \nhuman consideration and remedies for adverse decisions made using AI; \n(v) specific Federal Government uses of AI that are presumed by default \nto impact rights or safety; \n(vi) recommendations to agencies to reduce barriers to the responsible \nuse of AI, including barriers related to information technology infrastruc-\nture, data, workforce, budgetary restrictions, and cybersecurity processes; \n(vii) requirements that agencies identified in 31 U.S.C. 901(b) develop \nAI strategies and pursue high-impact AI use cases; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 23:02 Oct 31, 2023 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00030 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01NOE0.SGM 01NOE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 29 of 36 ===\n75219 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 210 / Wednesday, November 1, 2023 / Presidential Documents \n(viii) in consultation with the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of \nHomeland Security, and the heads of other appropriate agencies as deter-\nmined by the Director of OMB, recommendations to agencies regarding: \n(A) external testing for AI, including AI red-teaming for generative AI, \nto be developed in coordination with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure \nSecurity Agency; \n(B) testing and safeguards against discriminatory, misleading, inflam-\nmatory, unsafe, or deceptive outputs, as well as against producing child \nsexual abuse material and against producing non-consensual intimate im-\nagery of real individuals (including intimate digital depictions of the body \nor body parts of an identifiable individual), for generative AI; \n(C) reasonable steps to watermark or otherwise label output from genera-\ntive AI; \n(D) application of the mandatory minimum risk-management practices \ndefined under subsection 10.1(b)(iv) of this section to procured AI; \n(E) independent evaluation of vendors’ claims concerning both the effec-\ntiveness and risk mitigation of their AI offerings; \n(F) documentation and oversight of procured AI; \n(G) maximizing the value to agencies when relying on contractors to \nuse and enrich Federal Government data for the purposes of AI develop-\nment and operation; \n(H) provision of incentives for the continuous improvement of procured \nAI; and \n(I) training on AI in accordance with the principles set out in this \norder and in other references related to AI listed herein; and \n(ix) requirements for public reporting on compliance with this guidance."},{"char_end":120156,"char_start":119789,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":120156,"context_char_start":119789,"line":1739,"pdf_page":29,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; and \n(ii) within 180 days of the issuance of the guidance, the Director of \nOMB shall develop an initial means to ensure that agency contracts for \nthe acquisition of AI systems and services align with the guidance de-\nscribed in subsection 10.1(b) of this section and advance the other aims \nidentified in section 7224(d)(1) of the Advancing American AI Act (Public \nLaw 117–263, div."},{"char_end":121688,"char_start":121422,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":121688,"context_char_start":121422,"line":1762,"pdf_page":29,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(e) To improve transparency for agencies’ use of AI, the Director of OMB \nshall, on an annual basis, issue instructions to agencies for the collection, \nreporting, and publication of agency AI use cases, pursuant to section 7225(a) \nof the Advancing American AI Act."},{"char_end":121934,"char_start":121689,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":121934,"context_char_start":121689,"line":1765,"pdf_page":29,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(a) Within 45 days of the date \nof this order, to plan a national surge in AI talent in the Federal Government, \nthe Director of OSTP and the Director of OMB, in consultation with the \nAssistant to the President for National Security Affairs, the Assistant to \nthe President for Economic Policy, the Assistant to the President and Domes-\ntic Policy Advisor, and the Assistant to the President and Director of the \nGender Policy Council, shall identify priority mission areas for increased \nFederal Government AI talent, the types of talent that are highest priority \nto recruit and develop to ensure adequate implementation of this order \nand use of relevant enforcement and regulatory authorities to address AI \nrisks, and accelerated hiring pathways."},{"char_end":128531,"char_start":127693,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":128531,"context_char_start":127693,"line":1850,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"(b) Within 45 days of the date of this order, to coordinate rapid advances \nin the capacity of the Federal AI workforce, the Assistant to the President \nand Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy, in coordination with the Director \nof OSTP and the Director of OMB, and in consultation with the National \nCyber Director, shall convene an AI and Technology Talent Task Force, \nwhich shall include the Director of OPM, the Director of the General Services \nAdministration’s Technology Transformation Services, a representative from \nthe Chief Human Capital Officers Council, the Assistant to the President \nfor Presidential Personnel, members of appropriate agency technology talent \nprograms, a representative of the Chief Data Officer Council, and a representa-\ntive of the interagency council convened under subsection 10.1(a) of this \nsection."},{"char_end":129601,"char_start":128532,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":129601,"context_char_start":128532,"line":1861,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"The Task Force’s purpose shall be to accelerate and track the hiring \nof AI and AI-enabling talent across the Federal Government, including \nthrough the following actions: \n(i) within 180 days of the date of this order, tracking and reporting \nprogress to the President on increasing AI capacity across the Federal \nGovernment, including submitting to the President a report and rec-\nommendations for further increasing capacity; \n(ii) identifying and circulating best practices for agencies to attract, hire, \nretain, train, and empower AI talent, including diversity, inclusion, and \naccessibility best practices, as well as to plan and budget adequately \nfor AI workforce needs; \n(iii) coordinating, in consultation with the Director of OPM, the use of \nfellowship programs and agency technology-talent programs and human- \ncapital teams to build hiring capabilities, execute hires, and place AI \ntalent to fill staffing gaps; and \n(iv) convening a cross-agency forum for ongoing collaboration between \nAI professionals to share best practices and improve retention."},{"char_end":130290,"char_start":129603,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":130290,"context_char_start":129603,"line":1878,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall"],"text":"(c) Within 45 days of the date of this order, to advance existing Federal \ntechnology talent programs, the United States Digital Service, Presidential \nInnovation Fellowship, United States Digital Corps, OPM, and technology \ntalent programs at agencies, with support from the AI and Technology Talent \nTask Force described in subsection 10.2(b) of this section, as appropriate \nand permitted by law, shall develop and begin to implement plans to support \nthe rapid recruitment of individuals as part of a Federal Government-wide \nAI talent surge to accelerate the placement of key AI and AI-enabling talent \nin high-priority areas and to advance agencies’ data and technology strategies."},{"char_end":133646,"char_start":130292,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":133646,"context_char_start":130292,"line":1887,"pdf_page":31,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory; verify its scope against the complete source pages.","signals":["shall","shall"],"text":"(d) To meet the critical hiring need for qualified personnel to execute \nthe initiatives in this order, and to improve Federal hiring practices for \nAI talent, the Director of OPM, in consultation with the Director of OMB, \nshall: \n(i) within 60 days of the date of this order, conduct an evidence-based \nreview on the need for hiring and workplace flexibility, including Federal \nGovernment-wide direct-hire authority for AI and related data-science and \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 23:02 Oct 31, 2023 Jkt 262001 PO 00000 Frm 00033 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\01NOE0.SGM 01NOE0ddrumheller on DSK120RN23PROD with PRESDOC-E0\n=== PDF page 32 of 36 ===\n75222 Federal Register / Vol. 88, No. 210 / Wednesday, November 1, 2023 / Presidential Documents \ntechnical roles, and, where the Director of OPM finds such authority \nis appropriate, grant it; this review shall include the following job series \nat all General Schedule (GS) levels: IT Specialist (2210), Computer Scientist \n(1550), Computer Engineer (0854), and Program Analyst (0343) focused \non AI, and any subsequently developed job series derived from these \njob series; \n(ii) within 60 days of the date of this order, consider authorizing the \nuse of excepted service appointments under 5 CFR 213.3102(i)(3) to address \nthe need for hiring additional staff to implement directives of this order; \n(iii) within 90 days of the date of this order, coordinate a pooled-hiring \naction informed by subject-matter experts and using skills-based assess-\nments to support the recruitment of AI talent across agencies; \n(iv) within 120 days of the date of this order, as appropriate and permitted \nby law, issue guidance for agency application of existing pay flexibilities \nor incentive pay programs for AI, AI-enabling, and other key technical \npositions to facilitate appropriate use of current pay incentives; \n(v) within 180 days of the date of this order, establish guidance and \npolicy on skills-based, Federal Government-wide hiring of AI, data, and \ntechnology talent in order to increase access to those with nontraditional \nacademic backgrounds to Federal AI, data, and technology roles; \n(vi) within 180 days of the date of this order, establish an interagency \nworking group, staffed with both human-resources professionals and re-\ncruiting technical experts, to facilitate Federal Government-wide hiring \nof people with AI and other technical skills; \n(vii) within 180 days of the date of this order, review existing Executive \nCore Qualifications (ECQs) for Senior Executive Service (SES) positions \ninformed by data and AI literacy competencies and, within 365 days \nof the date of this order, implement new ECQs as appropriate in the \nSES assessment process; \n(viii) within 180 days of the date of this order, complete a review of \ncompetencies for civil engineers (GS–0810 series) and, if applicable, other \nrelated occupations, and make recommendations for ensuring that adequate \nAI expertise and credentials in these occupations in the Federal Govern-\nment reflect the increased use of AI in critical infrastructure; and \n(ix) work with the Security, Suitability, and Credentialing Performance \nAccountability Council to assess mechanisms to streamline and accelerate \npersonnel-vetting requirements, as appropriate, to support AI and fields \nrelated to other critical and emerging technologies."},{"char_end":133935,"char_start":133648,"classification":"clause_candidate","context_char_end":133935,"context_char_start":133648,"line":1935,"pdf_page":32,"reason":"Command-like sentence has substantive text outside submitted inventory;
